body:
## Summary

Owner direction, 2026-10-23: add and execute recurring testing, architecture/requirements reconciliation, bug fixing and evidence-based refactoring checkpoints before feature accumulation hides drift.

Implement the checkpoint in the existing AMA Backlog Delivery Coordinator and the appropriate existing delivery documentation, then execute the first checkpoint on pinned current main. This complements per-PR tests and release gates; it does not replace them or require Azure for local learning.

## Source references

* docs/brds/agentic-retrofit-programme-brd.md
* docs/prds/zava-forward-retrofit-programme-demonstrator.md
* docs/adrs/ and docs/architecture/mvp-to-src-parity-matrix.md
* .github/agents/ama-backlog-delivery-coordinator.agent.md
* Related governance #123, existing release gates #126 and journey experiments #129.
* Current feedback-first slices #344, #349, #350 and #360.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Recurring checkpoints trigger before epic closure, after every completed feature wave (at most eight active issues), and earlier after a material requirements/architecture change or significant regression. Record the covered issues, merged PRs, main SHA and requirement/ADR versions. Scope test breadth to the affected integration surface, not an unconditional full suite after every edit.
- [ ] Reconcile BRD/PRD requirement IDs and approved plan/ADR decisions with code, tests, delivered journeys and remaining backlog. Separate local observed, Azure observed, implemented but unverified, deferred, blocked and unknown; merged issue counts and redirects are not acceptance.
- [ ] Use a local-first ladder: focused regression/unit/static checks, affected-package suites, then local cross-package HTTP/browser and SQL Server/container integration as relevant. Run the smallest failing reproduction first in fix loops. Run required final full gates once the correction candidate is stable; do not waive them or rerun them ceremonially after each edit.
- [ ] Reserve Azure integration for explicitly listed Azure-only residuals after relevant local checks pass, with valid authority, complete cost headroom, finite plan and cleanup boundaries. Deferred Azure checks remain unverified, not passed; local engineering can proceed without tenant or cost clearance.
- [ ] Assess architectural boundaries, contracts, persistence, auth/roles, resident consent and human-approval boundaries, AI failure/manual paths, and regression-prone cross-feature journeys. Identify necessary refactoring from evidence, preserve behavior, and require a regression test for each confirmed behavior bug.
- [ ] Execute the first current-main checkpoint now: persist actual command results, traceability and architectural findings, limitations and a continue/fix/pivot recommendation in existing project evidence. Cover the current feedback-first journey and affected package boundaries; distinguish broad product acceptance from this bounded engineering checkpoint.
- [ ] Triage confirmed findings into deduplicated, independently scoped RPI bug/refactor issues with severity, reproduction, requirement/ADR links, acceptance criteria and explicit dependencies. Gate affected epic closure/dependent feature expansion on blocking findings only; independent work continues. Owner approval is required for requirement changes, architectural pivots and deliberate deferrals.
- [ ] Deliver genuine research, plan/details, changes and independent review artifacts in the PR. Treat the coordinator change as a Major HVE Builder behavior change with static review, behavior testing and host validation. Record actual unresolved blockers; no unsupported acceptance ticks or issue closure.

## Dependencies and execution boundaries

Parent: #123 (hierarchy, not ordering). No live tenant, deployed parity or Azure activation prerequisite for the local checkpoint. Reuse #126/#129 rather than claiming their operational or human-study criteria.

An existing #349 full gate owns the heavy lock. Do not interrupt, edit its worktree, reuse its output for a different head, or duplicate it. Read-only research may proceed in a new isolated worktree while it runs; coordinate local heavy tests after it releases the lock. Keep cap eight and existing safety/financial gates.

No new feature code, unrelated refactoring, private datasets, secrets, paid model calls or Azure mutations are authorized by this checkpoint. Confirmed code fixes get their own isolated RPI loop, branch and PR. Keep the primary dirty checkout untouched.
title: test(delivery): add recurring stabilization gates and execute first checkpoint
